facts.fact_text: On 21 August 2003 the non-governmental organisation "City-wide public council for the protection of citizens' rights in town planning and for the protection of the environment" decided to hold an assembly of Krylatskoye district residents at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square in Moscow.
One purpose of the planned assembly was to protest against the Moscow mayor's failure to respond to the resolution of the assembly held in May 2003.
One purpose of the planned assembly was to protest against the planned construction of several luxurious blocks of flats in the place of facilities for sports and children.
One purpose of the planned assembly was to cast a vote of no confidence in the city authorities and call for their resignation.
One purpose of the planned assembly was to discuss matters of local self-governance.
On 4 September 2003 a few dozen residents gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square.
The applicant was among the residents who gathered on the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003.
No loud speakers were deployed at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003.
No attempts were made to start a general discussion at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003.
The police dispersed the crowd at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square on 4 September 2003 by force.
At a nearby crossing, the police blocked the applicant's car.
The police held the driver of the applicant's car at gun-point.
The police took the applicant out of the car by force.
The police escorted the applicant to Krylatskoye district police station (ОВД района «Крылатское»).
At Krylatskoye district police station the applicant was placed in a cell.
The applicant remained in the cell at Krylatskoye district police station until he was brought before a judge on 5 September 2003.
The cell at Krylatskoye district police station was dirty and covered with spittle.
The applicant was not given any food or drink while detained at Krylatskoye district police station.
On 5 September 2003 the applicant was brought before a judge of the Kuntsevskiy District Court of Moscow.

On 25 August 2003 the applicant, together with three other co-organisers of the assembly, informed the Prefecture of the Western Administrative District of Moscow of the date, time, place and purposes of the assembly.
On 29 August 2003 the prefect of the Western Administrative District of Moscow issued a decision to accept the notice of the planned assembly.
On 3 September 2003 the prefect of the Western Administrative District of Moscow cancelled his previous decision of 29 August 2003 accepting the notice of the planned assembly.

The prefect cancelled his decision of 29 August 2003 "in connection with the operative information of law-enforcement authorities about an expected outbreak of terrorist activities in the Krylatskoye district and with a view to ensuring the safety of the district's residents".

Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, the executive body could refuse to accept the notice if the purpose of the assembly was contrary to the principles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, generally accepted public morals, if there was no undertaking on the part of the organisers to ensure public safety, if the assembly coincided in time and place with another one, if it threatened normal functioning of companies or organisations, or if it required suspending public or rail transport (§ 4).

Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, the executive body, in cooperation with the organisers, could suggest a different place, time or route of the assembly in order to ensure public safety (§ 5).
Under the provisional regulations approved by Presidential Decree no. 765 of 24 May 1993, refusal to accept notice of an assembly was amenable to judicial review (§ 10).

The Kuntsevskiy District Court established that the prefect had issued the contested decision of 3 September 2003 further to a letter from the head of the police command of the Western Administrative District of 2 September 2003.

In the letter of 2 September 2003, the head of the police command of the Western Administrative District asked the prefect to annul his decision of 29 August 2003 because the police command "had received, from various sources, information about potential terrorist attacks in Moscow, in places of mass gatherings".

The prefect cancelled his decision of 29 August 2003 "in connection with the operative information of law-enforcement authorities about an expected outbreak of terrorist activities in the Krylatskoye district and with a view to ensuring the safety of the district's residents".
On 3 September 2003 the police were instructed "to take measures to prevent the assembly planned for 4 September 2003 at the Zashchitnikov Neba Square from being held".

In the letter of 2 September 2003, the head of the police command of the Western Administrative District asked the prefect to annul his decision of 29 August 2003 because the police command "had received, from various sources, information about potential terrorist attacks in Moscow, in places of mass gatherings".

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that no evidence contradicting the information contained in the letter from the police command of the Western Administrative District to the prefect of the Western Administrative District had been produced before the court.

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that the prefect's decision of 3 September 2003 was issued not in connection with the notice filed by the assembly organisers but in connection with a threat of increasing terrorist activities in the areas of mass gatherings, with a view to ensuring the security of the Krylatskoye District's residents.

The Kuntsevskiy District Court found that the actions of the Krylatskoye district police, which were aimed at preventing the mass action from taking place in connection with a real threat to life, health and security of citizens, were compatible with the Moscow regulations on co-ordinated police action during mass assemblies and the requirements of Article 17 § 3 of the Russian Constitution.
